newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money edges down 60 bps to 10.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money edges down 60 bps to 10.7 pct.

text.p: Croatia's average money market rate edged down to 10.7 pct from 11.3 pct on Tuesday in thin trade caused by weaker demand for fresh funds, dealers said.
They put the total daily trade at modest 11.2 million kuna, of which only 4.4 million kuna were fresh loans.
For the first time in days offer overstripped the demand and all borrowers' demands for loans were met, leaving a surplus of 6.8 million kuna at the end of trading.
The overall call money rate edged up to 10 pct from 9.6 pct and dealers said some call money borrowings were made at a higher rate of 11 percent.
A smaller three-month loan was struck at the rate of 16 percent and one 6-10 days loan at 12 pct.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Wednesday at 5.3626 from 5.3679 to the dollar and at 3.5670 from 3.5646 to the German mark.
